answer: Follow the money's family tree. Every identity needs a first coin and eventually sweeps its earnings somewhere. The ledger traces both ends: identities seeded from one wallet, or whose payouts ripple back into one sink, form a cluster that shares a single reward. Like saffron, a farm's funding stains every alias it touches. To dodge this, an operator must fund and cash out each alias through separate, unlinked paths, paying fees and delay per alias; even an ember of shared history links them. Assumption: payouts vest 3 epochs, so a fast launder-and-sweep stands out.
